check.population: every binding the runtime resolves: handlers, plugins, services, formatters and policies
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a registered module, a discovery pattern or the configuration changes
check.refusal: startup validation or the composition-root test fails when a declared binding resolves to nothing
check.observation: the resolved bindings reported at startup, compared with the modules on disk and the configuration
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the modules on disk and the configuration, which the bindings reported at startup are compared against

distinctFrom.reason: Runtime discovery finds which components exist, while a capability declaration states what each one supports.
Runtime discovery finds components by convention or pattern, while introspection reads one object's type and members.
Runtime discovery finds and registers components, while reflection reads and acts on type metadata, which discovery may use.
Runtime discovery finds in-process components at startup, while service discovery resolves a service name to a network endpoint at call time.
Runtime discovery decides the component set as the program starts, while static analysis reasons about source that has not run.

records.name: Runtime Discovery
records.definition: A mechanism that finds the available handlers, plugins or services at startup by matching a naming convention, a file pattern or metadata, and registers each one it finds in place of a hand-written list.

exemplar.after:
const modules = await discover<HandlerModule>("./handlers/*.handler.js");
const handlers = modules.map(module => module.create());

distinctFrom.reason: Service discovery resolves a name to a healthy endpoint, while failover switches traffic to a standby when the active one fails.
Service discovery resolves endpoints, while health checks report whether each endpoint is ready.
Service discovery is the lookup at call time, while the service registry is the table the lookup reads.

records.name: Service Discovery
records.definition: A mechanism that resolves a service name to a healthy network endpoint at call time through a registry.

exemplar.after:
const endpoint = await serviceDiscovery.resolve("foo-service");
await http.get(new URL(`/foo/${id}`, endpoint));

distinctFrom.reason: Dynamic binding picks an implementation at runtime, while a capability declaration lists what an implementation supports so the pick can be checked.
Polymorphism lets the receiver choose the implementation per call, while dynamic binding chooses it from configuration or a registry.
Dynamic binding is the choice made at runtime, while a service registry is the keyed table it can choose from.

records.name: Dynamic Binding
records.definition: A mechanism that selects the implementation behind an interface at runtime, from configuration or a registry, so the choice is made at bootstrap or first use rather than fixed in code.

records.name: Dynamic Dispatch
records.definition: A mechanism that chooses which operation runs from the receiver or a keyed table at runtime, replacing a conditional over kinds.

distinctFrom.reason: Runtime extensibility adds capability through extension points, while stable interfaces keep those points unchanged across releases.
Extensibility is adding behavior with little change to existing code, while runtime extensibility adds it to a system that is already running.

records.name: Runtime Extensibility
records.definition: The degree to which new capability can be added to a running system through extension points, without modifying its core.
